title: Mike and the Star in the Pond
synopsis: A little otter watches a star appear and disappear in a pond, then notices how the surface changes its reflection.

related_resources.reason: Linder and Eckhoff (2020), person- and process-oriented observation questions: observing first, not demanding an approved answer.
CDC 3-year milestones (2026), More Parenting Tips and Activities: asking about stories and observations with caregivers.

rationale_citations.editorial_rationale: A small mystery opens a chance to wonder without making the character mistaken or foolish.
rationale_citations.evidence_scope: These are caregiver/education practice sources relevant to the narrative approach; they did not study this story or establish a causal effect.

rationale_citations.story_anchor:
A slow current carried it past the willow's reflection.

There, in the dark water beside the leaf, the little light appeared again.
rationale_citations.editorial_rationale: The character watches a change and revisits the same location; the water setting remains fictional, not an unsupervised water activity.
rationale_citations.evidence_scope: These are caregiver/education practice sources relevant to the narrative approach; they did not study this story or establish a causal effect.

source_note: Original fiction; caregiver sources justify only broad age-appropriate editorial decisions, not learning or sleep outcomes, and not imaginary biology or sky physics.
